thread:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression after landing flash-variant-2 routing for short-seq workloads. Throughput down ~10% on our 8k token long-running chat tests.

matt: Ugh. Is it consistently reproducible on canary?

anya: Yes on canary and a couple customer VMs. Quick profile points: kernel selector chooses flash-v2 for seq <= 64, but we see more L2 stalls and the runtime falls back to paged_attn on some shards.

rachel: Any KV cache layout changes in that CL? I remember ken touching interleaved packing earlier.

ken: I did a small change to interleaved packing stride to reduce padding for bf16. It should be a no-op for aligned pages, but maybe corner case.

anya: Attaching a short dump from perf and the selector log:
```
[selector] model=vicuna-13b seq=32 dtype=bfloat16 chosen=flash-v2 fallback=paged_attn reason=bank_conflict_detected
[perf] tokens/s baseline=1150 canary=1035 (-10.1%)
[profiling] l2_miss_rate +12%, warp_serialization increased, sm_efficiency down 7%
```

matt: bank_conflict_detected? That sounds like memory alignment/stride issue. Does flash-v2 assume packed KV layout contiguous per-head?

ken: flash-v2 assumes per-head contiguous KV with 64-byte alignment. Our interleaved layout keeps head0/1/2 continuous but reduces per-head stride in packed pages. If a page starts unaligned for bf16 we can get half-warp straddling.

rachel: Could dtype promotion/quantization path trigger different packing? e.g., when bf16 vs fp16 we change element size and forget to realign pages?

anya: Exactly. In the repro we saw model serving with bf16 enabled, and a small change in page allocator caused the page base to shift by 16 bytes occasionally. That makes 64b alignment -> 48b in practice.

ken: That explains bank conflicts. Flash kernels are sensitive to 64B lanes. Paged kernel tolerates misalignment but with higher overhead, so selector falling back reduces throughput.

matt: Action items: (1) add an assert in page allocator to keep 64B alignment for interleaved layouts, (2) add a fastpath in selector to prefer paged_attn only if fallback observed repeatedly, (3) run microbench across dtype {bf16,fp16} and seq {8,16,32,64}.

anya: Agreed. Also adding a selector trace metric so we can histogram fallbacks per-model.

rachel: For the short term can we revert ken's stride reduction? Might be safest while we patch the allocator.

ken: Will push a revert PR and tests. Also adding a unit that simulates page base offsets (+16, -16) to catch this.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for flash-variant-2 on pool: gpu-c2 (auto-paused due to perf regression alert).

ci-bot: perf-ci: queued microbench run (seqs=8,16,32,64; dtypes=bf16,fp16) — expecting ~4h.

anya: Thanks. Once CI confirms revert fixes, we'll unpause canary and maybe gate flash-v2 until we have alignment checks in allocator and a selector telemetry. :thumbsup:

matt: Feel free to @me on the PR. I'll help with the selector histogram and fallback throttling heuristic.

ken: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4821 - reverting stride-change, adding allocator assert + unit test.

anya: Great. I'll monitor canary after the revert. If anyone sees a similar customer report, add it to the thread.

rachel: Noted. Adding a runbook blurb about alignment sensitivity for flash kernels.

anya: End-of-thread plan: revert landed, CI green, add allocator assert, selector histo + throttling, re-run canary.
